summary: Confirmed DONE (60633eff3). The blocking ensureRates (old UsageService.ts:243-283, awaited inside scanSemaphore) was replaced by stale-while-revalidate pricing. startRatesRefresh loads disk rates, then forks one single-flight fetchRates into serviceScope, off the scan permit, when the rates are older than 24 h and no attempt was made in the last hour. fetchRates records ratesLastAttemptAtMs before the request, so failures, timeouts, non-200 responses and captive-portal HTML all back off for 1 h, and old rates stay in place. A summary waits only when no rates exist at all, at most 2 s, and that wait overlaps source discovery. ratesGeneration is bumped only when the document hash changes, and it is part of the transcript-source memo fingerprint. Pricing runs per slot at summary time, never inside the per-file scan cache, so fresh rates re-price memoized and cached data. A 30 s post-boot warm-up refreshes stale rates when a pricing cache exists. A test covers the main behaviour: with a hanging download and stale cache, two summaries come back in under 2 s, priced from the cache, with one fetch; with no cache and failing downloads, three summaries make one fetch. No other network fetch exists in the usage path, and the Hub has no counterpart. The leftover gaps are minor.

evidence.note: startRatesRefresh: single-flight through the ratesRefresh Deferred, with no yield between the re-check and the assignment. It skips the fetch within RATES_TTL_MS (24 h) or RATES_RETRY_MS (1 h) of the last attempt, and runs fetchRates via Effect.forkIn(serviceScope), so it is not interrupted when the caller goes away and does not hold the scan permit.

fetchRates sets ratesLastAttemptAtMs = now before the request, so every outcome (failure, timeout, empty or HTML body) backs off. The 10 s timeout covers the body read. On failure the old rates stay and state becomes cached/unavailable. On success it bumps the generation only when the revision changes and writes pricing-cache.json atomically.
readSummaryUnlocked starts the refresh, plans sources, and awaits the refresh only when rates.size === 0, with timeoutOption(max(0, 2000 - waitedMs)).
Constants: RATES_RETRY_MS 1 h, RATES_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS 10 s, RATES_FIRST_FETCH_WAIT_MS 2 s, RATES_WARM_DELAY_MS 30 s.
The memo fingerprint includes pricing.generation, so new rates invalidate memoized transcript sources.
UsageSlotAggregator prices slots with the request's rates when a summary runs (priceUsageSlot), so the scan cache holds no frozen prices and a generation bump fully re-prices the data.
Boot warm-up: after 30 s, if pricing-cache.json exists, it calls startRatesRefresh in the background.
scanSemaphore.withPermits(1) wraps readSummaryUnlocked. The only network work inside it is a bounded 2 s wait, and only when there are no rates at all.
Test: with a stale cache and a hanging download, summaries return in under 2 s with cached pricing and one fetch. With no cache and failing downloads, three summaries make one fetch.

fixDefects: None that bring back the reported cost. Minor gaps: (1) The 10 s RATES_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS (UsageService.ts:89, applied at 402-409) still covers the 2.75 MB body read even though the fetch now runs in the background. On links slower than about 2.2 Mbit/s it always times out: rates never refresh, a fresh install stays 'unavailable', and a partial download is retried each hour a summary is opened. (2) No test covers the generation-bump path, where a background refresh with a new revision re-prices an already memoized source. Only the stale-cache and back-off paths are tested. (3) The back-off is a fixed 1 h kept in memory, and the warm-up is a fixed 30 s delay rather than an idle check. Both are acceptable. (4) A legacy or corrupt pricing-cache.json, while offline, is re-read and JSON-parsed on every summary inside the permit, because loadRatesFromDisk only short-circuits once ratesFetchedAtMs is set. This is cheap and rare.
implementationSketch: Optional polish: in UsageService.fetchRates, raise the background timeout (for example 60 s, or a separate connect/first-byte timeout) now that nothing waits on it beyond the 2 s first-fetch cap. Add a UsageService.test.ts case: stale cache with document A, an HttpClient stub that answers document B after a Deferred is released, readSummary (expect cached pricing from A), release the stub and wait for the refresh, readSummary again and expect B's cost and state 'live'. Also check that an unchanged document keeps the memo hit (parsedFileCount 0). Optionally remember a failed disk parse (a flag set in loadRatesFromDisk) so a bad cache file is not re-read on every summary.
decisionReason: Server-local usage pricing only. No auth, E2EE, Hub protocol or hosted lifecycle impact.
